subject: Chemistry
title: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques
summary: Carbon forms four bonds (tetravalency), long chains (catenation) and multiple bonds. Hybridisation (sp³, sp², sp) decides shape and bond angles.

Electron displacement effects — inductive (σ bonds), resonance/mesomeric (π systems), hyperconjugation and electromeric effect — explain the stability of carbocations, carbanions and free radicals and the strength of acids and bases.
Reactions happen when nucleophiles (electron-rich) attack electrophiles (electron-poor). Bonds break homolytically (free radicals) or heterolytically (ions).
Purification (crystallisation, distillation, chromatography), qualitative tests (Lassaigne's test) and quantitative estimation (Dumas, Kjeldahl, Carius, Liebig) are the practical side of the chapter.

formulas.name: Hybridisation from bonds
formulas.when: Shape and bond angle at a carbon.
formulas.mistake: Count σ bonds (and lone pairs) around the atom, not the total number of bonds.

formulas.name: Degree of unsaturation (DBE)
formulas.when: Rings + π bonds from a molecular formula.
formulas.note: Ignore O and S; treat halogens like H.

formulas.name: Inductive effect
formulas.formula: −I: NO₂ > CN > F > Cl > Br > I > OH;  +I: (CH₃)₃C > (CH₃)₂CH > CH₃CH₂ > CH₃
formulas.note: The inductive effect fades quickly with distance (beyond ~3 carbons it is negligible).

formulas.name: Resonance (mesomeric) effect
formulas.when: Stability of conjugated species, directing effects.

formulas.name: C–H bond dissociation energy
formulas.formula: sp C–H > sp² C–H > sp³ C–H  (more s-character → shorter, stronger bond);  allylic/benzylic C–H weakest (gives a resonance-stabilised radical)
formulas.note: Weaker C–H ⇔ more stable radical formed (same order as free-radical stability).

formulas.name: Carbanion stability
formulas.formula: CH₃⁻ > 1° > 2° > 3° (opposite of carbocations); stabilised by −I/−R groups and sp character

formulas.name: Hyperconjugation
formulas.formula: more α-hydrogens → more hyperconjugation → greater stability
formulas.note: It explains why 3° carbocations and more substituted alkenes are more stable.

formulas.name: Kjeldahl's method
formulas.formula: % N = (1.4 × N_acid × V_acid used)/mass of compound
formulas.mistake: Not for nitro, azo compounds or N in a ring (pyridine).

formulas.name: Carius method
formulas.formula: % X = (atomic mass of X × mass of AgX)/(molar mass of AgX × mass of compound) × 100;  % S via BaSO₄

formulas.name: Liebig's method (C and H)
formulas.formula: % C = (12/44) × (mass CO₂/mass compound) × 100;  % H = (2/18) × (mass H₂O/mass compound) × 100

examples.title: Kjeldahl
examples.problem: 0.5 g of a compound gives NH₃ that neutralises 10 mL of 1 M H₂SO₄. % N?
examples.solution: 10 mL of 1 M H₂SO₄ neutralises 0.02 mol NH₃ = 0.28 g N. % N = 56%.

examples.title: Carius
examples.problem: 0.20 g of a compound gives 0.287 g AgCl. % Cl?

examples.title: Liebig
examples.problem: 0.30 g of a compound gives 0.44 g CO₂. % C?

examples.title: Acid strength
examples.solution: Cl₂CHCOOH > FCH₂COOH > ClCH₂COOH > CH₃COOH — more and stronger −I groups stabilise the carboxylate ion.

examples.title: Lassaigne's test
examples.problem: A sodium fusion extract gives a blood-red colour with FeCl₃. Which elements are present?
examples.solution: Both N and S: they form NaSCN, which gives blood-red [Fe(SCN)]²⁺. N alone gives Prussian blue; S alone gives violet with sodium nitroprusside.

topics.title: Classification and homologous series
topics.explain: Organic compounds are acyclic (open chain: alkanes, alkenes, alkynes) or cyclic — alicyclic (cyclohexane) or aromatic (benzenoid like benzene, non-benzenoid like tropolone, and heterocyclic like pyridine, furan). They are also grouped by functional group. A homologous series is a family with the same functional group in which successive members differ by –CH₂– (14 u): same general formula (alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkenes CₙH₂ₙ, alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, alcohols CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH), similar chemical properties, and physical properties (boiling point) that change gradually with molar mass.

topics.title: IUPAC nomenclature
topics.explain: Find the longest chain containing the principal functional group, number it to give that group the lowest locant, name substituents alphabetically. Priority of suffixes: –COOH > –SO₃H > –COOR > –COCl > –CONH₂ > –CN > –CHO > >C=O > –OH > –NH₂ > C=C > C≡C.

topics.title: Isomerism
topics.explain: Structural: chain, position, functional group, metamerism, tautomerism (keto–enol). Stereoisomerism: geometrical (cis/trans across C=C or in rings) and optical (chiral carbon, non-superimposable mirror images).

topics.title: Bond fission and reactive intermediates
topics.explain: Homolytic fission gives free radicals (in light/peroxides); heterolytic fission gives carbocations and carbanions. Carbocations are planar (sp²), carbanions pyramidal (sp³), free radicals planar.

topics.title: Nucleophiles and electrophiles
topics.explain: Nucleophiles: OH⁻, CN⁻, NH₃, H₂O, ROH (lone pairs or negative charge). Electrophiles: H⁺, NO₂⁺, carbocations, BF₃, AlCl₃ (electron-deficient). Reactions: substitution, addition, elimination, rearrangement.

topics.title: Electromeric effect
topics.explain: A temporary, complete shift of π electrons to one atom when a reagent approaches — operates only in the presence of the reagent (unlike the permanent inductive and resonance effects).

topics.title: Purification methods
topics.explain: Crystallisation (solubility difference), sublimation (camphor, naphthalene), simple distillation (large bp difference), fractional distillation (close bp), distillation under reduced pressure (decomposes at bp), steam distillation (steam-volatile, immiscible — aniline), differential extraction, and chromatography (adsorption or partition; Rf = distance by compound/distance by solvent).

topics.title: Qualitative analysis
topics.explain: Sodium fusion (Lassaigne) converts N, S, X to NaCN, Na₂S, NaX. N: Prussian blue with FeSO₄ + FeCl₃. S: black PbS with lead acetate, violet with nitroprusside. Halogens: AgNO₃ after boiling with HNO₃ (white AgCl soluble in NH₃, pale-yellow AgBr, yellow AgI). Br vs I (layer test): sodium-fusion extract + chlorine water + CHCl₃/CCl₄ — Cl₂ frees the halogen into the organic layer: violet = iodine, orange/brown = bromine.

ratta: −I: NO₂ > CN > F > Cl > Br > I;  +I: tert-butyl > isopropyl > ethyl > methyl.
Kjeldahl % N = 1.4 NV/w (not for nitro/azo/ring N).
N + S → blood red;  N → Prussian blue.
C–H BDE: sp > sp² > sp³;  allylic/benzylic C–H weakest.
Layer test (Cl₂ water + CHCl₃): violet = I, orange/brown = Br.
